responses.option-1: The contrapositive does more than reverse the statements: it also negates both of them. Compare the only way $p\to q$ can be false with the only way $\neg q\to\neg p$ can be false. You will find that both fail on the same assignment.
responses.option-2: No. An implication and its contrapositive have the same truth value on every assignment. The original $p\to q$ is false exactly when $p$ is true and $q$ is false. Those same values make the antecedent of $\neg q\to\neg p$ true and its consequent false; in every other case both implications are true.
